ready.description: How many of the organization's rows of the kind are ready and can be claimed now.

ids.description: The ids of the parked rows to redrive, at least one and at most 500.

attempt.description: How many attempts have been made on the row since it was enqueued or last redriven.

cancel.description: The cancellation requested for the row, present only when a request is recorded.

created_at.description: When the row was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

done_at.description: When the row was last done, cancelled, or parked, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none of those has happened since it was enqueued or last redriven.

first_enqueued_at.description: When the row's work was first enqueued, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, which a redrive does not change.

kind.description: The name of the row's kind.

last_error.description: The error the row last recorded, absent when none is recorded.

last_outcome.description: The outcome the row last recorded, such as transient, permanent, budget_exhausted, done, or redriven, absent when none is recorded.

lease.description: The worker's hold on the row, present only while the row is leased.

max_attempts.description: How many attempts the row may have before it is parked.

next_attempt_at.description: The earliest time the row's next attempt may start, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when no retry time is set.

status.description: The row's status: ready, leased, done, parked, or cancelled.

subject.description: What the row is about, in its kind's words, absent when the kind could not describe the row.

superseded_by.description: The id of the row that replaced this one, absent unless the row was superseded.

unique_key.description: The key that keeps a second row for the same work from being enqueued, absent when the row has none.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

status.description: Only rows with this status: ready, leased, done, parked, cancelled, or deferred, which is the ready rows that cannot be claimed yet; absent lists every status.

controls.description: Which operator controls the kind offers.

kind.description: The kind's name, which the kind's routes take in their path.

label.description: The kind's name for a person to read.

epoch.description: The boot count of the process that holds the row, absent when none is recorded.

expires_at.description: When the lease expires unless its holder renews it, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none is recorded.

generation.description: The lease's generation, a number that rises each time the row is claimed, redriven, or parked.

leased_at.description: When the row was claimed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none is recorded.

owner.description: The id of the Triage Factory process that holds the row.

oldest_ready_age_seconds.description: How old, in seconds from its first enqueue, the kind's oldest ready row may get before the kind's queue counts as behind.

redriven.description: How many of the named rows returned to ready; a row that was no longer parked is not counted.

detail.description: A longer description, such as the pull request's or issue's title, absent when it is unknown.

fields.description: Further facts about the row by name, such as event_type and entity_id.

label.description: A short name for what the row is about, such as owner/repo#18 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

superseded_by.description: The id of the organization's row of the same kind that replaces this one.

superseded.description: 1 when the row was settled as superseded, or 0 when it was no longer parked.

active.description: Whether this is the connection the organization uses in the workspace, which is the one whose events are processed.

app_name.description: The Slack app's bot name, empty when Slack gave none.

bot_user_id.description: The Slack user id of the app's bot.

connection.description: The app's live Socket Mode connection status, absent for an app that receives events over HTTP and before the first connection attempt.

connected_at.description: When the connection last opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

consecutive_failures.description: How many connection attempts in a row have failed.

last_error.description: The error of the last failed attempt, absent when there is none.

last_event_at.description: When the connection last received an event, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

sightings.description: Workspaces the app received events from that have no connection in the organization, absent when there are none.

count.description: How many events arrived from the workspace.

last_seen.description: When the last of them arrived, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

state.description: The connection's state: dialing, open, draining, backing_off, or auth_failed.

created_at.description: When the connection was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

enterprise_id.description: The id of the Enterprise Grid organization the workspace belongs to, absent for a standalone workspace.

registered_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who connected the app, absent when that person has since been removed.

source.description: Whose Slack app the connection is through: org for an app the organization created, or deployment for the deployment's own app.

transport.description: How Slack delivers the app's events, socket or events_api, or null on a deployment connection, which uses the transport the deployment configures.

updated_at.description: When the connection was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

session.description: The session cookie a browser sign-in sets. A deployment served over plain HTTP names it sid.
session.name: __Host-sid

token.description: An API token, sent as Authorization: Bearer tf_….

get.description: Returns the avatar image of a person in the caller's organization. The image is fetched from the address the person's sign-in provider gave and cached for a short time.

parameters.description: The person's id.
parameters.name: user_id

post.description: Returns one page of the pull requests the caller's GitHub identity authored and those opened by runs the caller started, from what TF last polled, narrowed by the body's filters. In multi mode, when the caller has a GitHub identity bound, the read also starts a one-time background import of that identity's recent pull requests from GitHub, which adds them to TF.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

patch.description: Converts one of the caller's pull requests to a draft, or marks it ready for review, on GitHub, and returns the pull request as the list returns it. The pull request must be one POST /api/dashboard/prs/list returns to the caller.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request's entity, as the pull request list returns it.
parameters.name: entity_id

patch.summary: Update one of the caller's pull requests

get.description: Reads one of the caller's pull requests from GitHub and returns its mergeability, its reviewers' latest decisions, and its check runs. The pull request must be one POST /api/dashboard/prs/list returns to the caller.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request's entity, as the pull request list returns it.
parameters.name: entity_id

get.summary: Get a pull request's live status

get.description: Returns counts of the pull requests the caller's GitHub identity authored and the reviews it gave and received, with merges and closes counted within the window, from what TF last polled. Every count is 0 when the caller has no GitHub identity bound on the organization's host. In multi mode, when one is bound, the read also starts a one-time background import of that identity's recent pull requests from GitHub, which adds them to TF.

parameters.description: Start of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; absent is the last 30 days.
parameters.name: since

get.summary: Get the caller's pull request statistics

get.description: Returns one pull request or review a run prepared, with its kind-specific details. A pull request's title and body are read from GitHub, and so is the current head a pending review's comments are each compared against.

parameters.description: The deliverable's id.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Publishes a deliverable a run prepared: a draft pull request is marked ready for review on GitHub, and a pending review is submitted to GitHub with its staged comments. The run that prepared it is told, and its task closes when this was the last deliverable awaiting a person on a run that completed.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request or review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

delete.description: Removes one inline comment staged on a pending review deliverable, so it is not posted when the review is approved.

parameters.description: The id of the review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The id of the staged comment, as the deliverable's details list it.
parameters.name: commentId

delete.summary: Delete a pending review's staged comment

patch.description: Replaces the text of one inline comment staged on a pending review deliverable. The comment reaches GitHub only when the review is approved.

parameters.description: The id of the review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The id of the staged comment, as the deliverable's details list it.
parameters.name: commentId

patch.summary: Edit a pending review's staged comment

get.description: Returns the unified diff of the pull request a deliverable is or reviews, read from GitHub: the pull request's current diff, or for a review with comments the diff as it stood when the run finished writing the review. When GitHub refuses the diff as too large, the body is reassembled from each file's patch and the X-Diff-Truncated response header says so.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request or review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The path of one file in the diff, to return that file's diff alone; absent returns every file.
parameters.name: file

post.description: Marks a draft pull request deliverable closed and closes its pull request on GitHub, keeping the branch. The run that prepared it is told, and its task closes when this was the last deliverable awaiting a person on a run that completed. A pending review is dismissed through PATCH /api/deliverables/{id}/review instead.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request deliverable.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Dismiss a draft pull request deliverable

patch.description: Writes a new title, body, or both to a pull request deliverable's pull request on GitHub, and records them on the deliverable once GitHub accepts them. A field the body leaves out keeps the value GitHub holds now, and a body naming neither field is refused.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request deliverable.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Deletes a draft pull request deliverable's head branch from the repository on GitHub, closes the pull request, and marks the deliverable closed; the branch delete cannot be undone. The run that prepared it is told, and its task closes when this was the last deliverable awaiting a person on a run that completed.

parameters.description: The id of the pull request deliverable.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Reject a draft pull request deliverable

patch.description: Stages a new summary body, event, or both on a pending review deliverable, which reach GitHub only when the review is approved, or dismisses the review with state set to dismissed. Dismissing tells the run that prepared the review, and closes its task when this was the last deliverable awaiting a person on a run that completed. Nothing is sent to GitHub.

parameters.description: The id of the review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

patch.summary: Edit or dismiss a pending review deliverable

post.description: Reads a pending review deliverable's pull request from GitHub and moves the review's staged comments onto its current head: a comment whose code moved follows it, and a comment whose code is gone is removed. Refused when that would leave a review with no summary body and no comments.

parameters.description: The id of the review deliverable.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Move a pending review to the pull request's head

post.description: Returns one page of the entities the caller may read, newest first, narrowed by the body's filters: the pull requests, issues, vulnerable packages, and Slack threads and messages in the repositories, projects, teams, and channels the caller's teams track. Each entity carries its newest event's type and time.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one entity the caller may read, in the shape the entity list returns it.

parameters.description: The entity's id.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Returns one page of the events recorded on the entities the caller may read, newest recorded first, narrowed by the body's filters. A page_token resumes after the last event of the page that returned it, so a walk neither repeats nor skips an event while new ones are recorded.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one event recorded on an entity the caller may read, in the shape the event list returns it.

parameters.description: The event's id.
parameters.name: id

get.description: Reports status ok once the server accepts requests. It needs no credential and checks no database or integration, so it says only that the process is serving.
get.summary: Check that the server is up

get.description: Returns the open Jira tickets of one team's tracked projects that have no task yet, in two lists: those assigned to the caller, and unassigned ones in a pickup status. A parent ticket with open subtasks is left out, and each ticket says which action its Jira status suggests.

parameters.description: The id of the team whose tracked Jira projects the deck draws from; when it is absent, or names a team the caller is not on, the deck is for the team the caller last wrote under, or else for their oldest team.
parameters.name: team_id

post.description: Assigns each named ticket on the caller's carry-over deck to the caller in Jira, moves it to its project's in-progress status, and creates a task the caller holds. A ticket the action cannot apply to is reported in results, and the others still apply.
post.summary: Claim Jira tickets from the carry-over deck

post.description: Moves each named ticket assigned to the caller to its project's done status in Jira and closes it in Triage Factory, creating no task. A ticket the action cannot apply to is reported in results, and the others still apply.
post.summary: Close Jira tickets from the carry-over deck

post.description: Creates a queued task for each named ticket on the caller's carry-over deck, without writing to Jira. A ticket the action cannot apply to is reported in results, and the others still apply.
post.summary: Queue Jira tickets from the carry-over deck

get.description: Returns the LLM spend of the runs the caller started in their current organization over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, model, and UTC day.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's Slack connections, active and inactive, ordered by workspace name, then workspace id, then app id. Each connection carries its Socket Mode status when it has one.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns the organization's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by team, person, category, model, and UTC day, and the spend attributed to no team.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

get.description: Returns every kind of durable work the deployment registers, with the operator controls each kind offers and its monitoring objective.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

get.summary: List the kinds of durable work

get.description: Returns how many of the organization's rows of the kind are ready, leased, parked, and deferred, and the ages of the oldest ready and deferred rows.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

get.summary: Get a work kind's queue depth

post.description: Records a cancellation request on each named row, which takes effect when the row is next claimed or its holder next renews its lease, and answers how many requests were recorded. A named row that has settled or already has a request is skipped, and a kind whose controls do not include cancel refuses the call.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's rows of the kind, newest first, optionally narrowed to one status. Each row carries its kind's description of what it is about.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Returns each named parked row to ready with a fresh attempt budget, and answers how many moved. A named row that is no longer parked is skipped, and a kind whose controls do not include redrive refuses the call.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

get.description: Returns one of the organization's rows of the kind, in any status, in the shape the list serves it.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: The row's id, a positive integer.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Settles the parked row as cancelled in favour of the named replacement row, which releases the row's unique key, and answers whether it did. A row that is no longer parked is left as it is, and a kind whose controls do not include supersede refuses the call.

parameters.description: The organization's id.
parameters.name: org_id

parameters.description: The work kind's name, as the catalogue lists it, such as event_queue.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: The row's id, a positive integer.
parameters.name: id

patch.description: Sets or clears the branch agents base their work on in the repository, and returns the repository with the change applied.

parameters.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Returns the open task for the entity, event type, and dedup key on the acting team, creating it when there is none, anchored on the newest matching event recorded on the entity. Answers 201 when it creates the task and 200 when it finds one. It starts no run; delegating the task is POST /api/tasks/{id}/delegate.

Returns the event types and entity kinds among the tasks the caller can see in a lane, the set the lane filters of POST /api/tasks/list describe, with how many tasks have each. It takes only those lane filters, and refuses the list's other fields and its paging fields by name.
post.summary: Count a lane's tasks by event type and entity kind

post.description: Returns one page of the tasks the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_key, or without one by attention and then priority. Each task says whether the caller may write it. A page_token resumes after the last task of the page that returned it, and is refused for different filters.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one task the caller can see, with whether the caller may write it and the teams the caller's claim or delegation of it may put it on.

parameters.description: The task's id.
parameters.name: id

patch.description: Closes the task as done or dismissed, snoozes it until a time, returns a snoozed task to the queue, or confirms in_progress on a task the caller holds, and returns the task with the change applied. Closing a task tells any run working on it that it closed; the run is not stopped.

parameters.description: The task's id.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Without target_user_id, the caller claims the task: it moves to in_progress under the caller, any run the agent had on it is stopped, and a Jira or Linear issue behind it is assigned to the caller and moved to in-progress. With target_user_id, the claim another person holds moves to that person, and nothing else changes. Returns the task with the claim applied.

parameters.description: The task's id.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Claim a task or hand it to another person

post.description: Hands the task to the team's agent and starts a run of the blueprint on it, stopping any run already working on the task, which keeps the deliverables it left. Returns the task's lane and version after the handoff and the run's first conversation.

parameters.description: The task's id.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Delegate a task to the agent

post.description: Puts the task back in the queue whatever its status, unclaimed, and returns it. It stops every run working on the task and ends its conversations, keeps the deliverables they left, and, where the claim moved a Jira or Linear issue to the claimant, unassigns the issue and moves it back to the status it had before.

parameters.description: The task's id.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Return a task to the queue

delete.description: Removes a person from the team. A caller who names their own id leaves the team, and the team's last admin cannot be removed.

parameters.description: The team's id.
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: The id of the person to remove.
parameters.name: user_id

get.description: Returns the team's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, event handler, model, and UTC day. The totals by person are included only for a team admin.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket that streams events for the caller in their current organization, such as a changed task list or a run's new messages. Most events say only that a resource changed, and the client reads it again through its route.
